routes.label: Derive the angle identities and count distinct cosine values

question:
Suppose \(a\) is a real number such that the equation

\[a\cdot(\sin x+\sin(2x))=\sin(3x)\]

has more than one solution in the interval \((0,\pi).\) The set of all such \(a\) can be written in the form \((p,q)\cup(q,r),\) where \(p,\) \(q,\) and \(r\) are real numbers with \(p\lt q\lt r.\) What is \(p+q+r?\)
solution:
On \((0,\pi)\), \(\sin x>0\), so dividing by \(\sin x\) can turn the equation into an algebraic equation in \(\cos x\).

The double-angle and angle-addition formulas give
\[
\sin(2x)=2\sin x\cos x
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin(3x)
&=\sin(2x)\cos x+\cos(2x)\sin x\\
&=2\sin x\cos^2x+(2\cos^2x-1)\sin x\\
&=\sin x(4\cos^2x-1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the original equation is equivalent to
\[
a(1+2\cos x)=4\cos^2x-1,
\]
or, after moving everything to one side and factoring,
\[
(2\cos x+1)(2\cos x-1-a)=0.
\]

The first factor gives \(\cos x=-\frac12\), hence \(x=\frac{2\pi}{3}\), for every \(a\). The second gives
\[
\cos x=\frac{a+1}{2}.
\]
As \(x\) moves through \((0,\pi)\), its point on the upper unit semicircle moves strictly from right to left. Consequently, \(\cos x\) takes each value in \((-1,1)\) exactly once. The second factor therefore supplies a solution precisely when
\[
-1<\frac{a+1}{2}<1,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad -3<a<1.
\]
This solution coincides with the first one exactly when
\[
\frac{a+1}{2}=-\frac12,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad a=-2.
\]

Hence there are two distinct solutions exactly for
\[
a\in(-3,-2)\cup(-2,1).
\]
Thus \(p=-3\), \(q=-2\), and \(r=1\), giving
\[
p+q+r=\boxed{-4},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The sum \(\sin x+\sin(2x)\) and the expression \(\sin(3x)\) share a half-angle sine factor. Exposing it identifies a solution that persists for every \(a\).

Put \(t=x/2\), so \(0<t<\pi/2\). Adding the angle-addition formulas for \(\sin(3t+t)\) and \(\sin(3t-t)\) gives
\[
\sin(4t)+\sin(2t)=2\sin(3t)\cos t.
\]
Also, \(\sin(6t)=2\sin(3t)\cos(3t)\). The equation therefore becomes
\[
2\sin(3t)\bigl(a\cos t-\cos(3t)\bigr)=0.
\]

Because \(0<3t<3\pi/2\), the first factor vanishes only at \(3t=\pi\). This gives \(t=\pi/3\), or \(x=2\pi/3\), for every \(a\).

For the other factor, let \(y=\cos t\). Then \(0<y<1\). Angle addition and the double-angle formulas give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\cos(3t)
&=(2\cos^2t-1)\cos t-2\sin^2t\cos t\\
&=4y^3-3y.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(a\cos t=\cos(3t)\) becomes
\[
ay=4y^3-3y.
\]
Since \(y>0\), this is equivalent to
\[
y^2=\frac{a+3}{4}.
\]
There is exactly one admissible \(y\in(0,1)\), and hence exactly one corresponding \(t\), precisely when \(-3<a<1\). This second solution equals the persistent solution \(t=\pi/3\) exactly when \(y=1/2\), which gives \(a=-2\).

The required set is therefore
\[
(-3,-2)\cup(-2,1),
\]
so
\[
p+q+r=-3-2+1=\boxed{-4},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Expose the shared sine factor
